record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Is there a timelike geodesically complete, inextendible Lorentzian manifold satisfying an energy condition and containing a partial Cauchy surface with a trapped surface?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Does there exist a Lorentzian manifold (M, g) of dimension at least 4 with the following properties simultaneously?

(i) (M, g) is time-oriented and inextendible (there is no isometric embedding of (M, g) as a proper open subset into a strictly larger connected time-oriented Lorentzian manifold of the same dimension).

(ii) (M, g) is timelike geodesically complete, i.e. every affinely parametrized timelike geodesic extends to all values of its affine parameter in R.

(iii) (M, g) satisfies a (non-trivial) energy condition such as the null energy condition Ric(v,v) ≥ 0 for all null vectors v, or the strong energy condition Ric(v,v) ≥ 0 for all timelike vectors v.

(iv) (M, g) contains an acausal, edgeless spacelike hypersurface Σ (a partial Cauchy surface).

(v) Σ contains a closed (compact without boundary) spacelike submanifold S of codimension 2 that is a trapped surface, meaning that both families of future-directed null geodesics issuing orthogonally from S have everywhere negative mean curvature (i.e., both null mean curvatures of S are everywhere negative).

Equivalently, does there exist an example showing that one cannot drop the global hyperbolicity hypothesis from Penrose-type singularity theorems while keeping inextendibility, an energy condition, a partial Cauchy surface, and a trapped surface, and still force timelike geodesic incompleteness?
artifact.status_search_result: Penrose-type singularity theorems show that a globally hyperbolic spacetime satisfying an energy condition and containing a noncompact Cauchy surface together with a trapped surface must be timelike geodesically incomplete. Without global hyperbolicity (only assuming a partial Cauchy surface) and with inextendibility imposed, the existence/nonexistence of such a complete example remains a recognized open question in mathematical relativity; recent surveys and rigidity results (e.g., on rigid singularity theorems and trapped sets in globally hyperbolic spacetimes) do not appear to resolve this version. No source found that explicitly closes the problem.

status_evidence.title: A critical appraisal of the singularity theorems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses hypotheses (global hyperbolicity, energy conditions, trapped surfaces) in Penrose/Hawking singularity theorems and open issues regarding completeness.
status_evidence.claim: Variants of Penrose's theorem and the role of partial Cauchy surfaces versus global hyperbolicity remain actively studied.

status_evidence.title: Rigid singularity theorem in globally hyperbolic spacetimes
status_evidence.snippet: A globally hyperbolic spacetime with SEC containing trapped sets is either timelike geodesically incomplete or splits isometrically.
status_evidence.claim: Rigid versions are known under global hyperbolicity, not under only a partial Cauchy surface assumption.

status_evidence.title: Spacetime singularities and curvature blow-ups
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems on completeness and singularities under various causality and energy hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of complete inextendible counterexamples under weakened causality remains discussed as open.
